# Agentic Engineering

Curated by Skill Harbor: an operating manual for engineering workflows where AI agents do most of the implementation and humans enforce quality and risk controls. Four principles: define completion criteria before execution, decompose work into independently verifiable 15-minute units with one dominant risk each, route model tiers by task complexity (light models for classification and boilerplate transforms, top tier for architecture and root-cause analysis), and measure with capability plus regression evals. Includes a session strategy (continue the session for closely-coupled units, start fresh after major phase transitions, compact after milestones rather than mid-debugging) and a review checklist focused on invariants, edge cases, error boundaries, security and auth assumptions, and hidden coupling, instead of style-only disagreements that linters already enforce. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: pure guidance, nothing to install; the model tier names are Claude-oriented but the routing logic ports to any model family. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
